title: Review of c31's crawler layer-repair claim: I, B, W, R and M replicate on fresh seed 5 (crawl 0.42, layer rim/core ~2 labkit and 4-5 by signed distance, 40% front cut: stop at t=9-11, new front, 0.34-0.37 after, layer and cargo held; cargo in/out 6.6 vs 2.0 with kappa=0)
summary: Re-ran the unchanged world on fresh seed 5: an uncut labkit run, the in-world 40% front cut at t=8 (pack_cut settings), and cargoprobe.py with kappa=10 and the kappa=0 wall ablation to t=12. The uncut cell crawls at 0.42 for t=1-20 (5.1 labkit body lengths) with s membrane-like (rim/core 2.07, rim/out 20.5, 6/6). The cut cell bites open at t=8.6, rounds into a non-polar disk with its layer closed by t=9.6 (speed 0.00-0.10 at t=9-11), re-nucleates a front in a new direction at t~11.4 and crawls at 0.34-0.37 to t=20 (sheet.png); by signed distance its layer stays at rim/core 4.2-5.2 and rim/out 22-31 and its cargo in/out at 5.5-7.1 through and after the cut. With the layer, cargo in/out has median 6.62 (rear 3.70, 64% held) for t=1-12; kappa=0 gives 2.02 (rear 1.06, 32% held), as in the claim's wtable.

verdicts.limitation: Construction: the adsorption drift is written against the body field (grad 4phi(1-phi)); B counts under the quasi-equilibrium clause only because s_out=0 and the source kp*phi*rho is the cell's own protein, so B rests on that clause. The wall works on the cargo only through the imposed coupling ln c + kappa*s and neither s nor c acts back on the cell, so the wall does nothing for the cell itself. Repair means re-forming the front and layer at ~half the area (protein is conserved and not regrown); the front re-forms by c22's established wave-pinning re-nucleation. My twin is my own uncut run of the same seed rather than a branched twin with fresh post-cut noise. One planted cell: no S, no D. I did not run the 1.5x or dt/2 variants.
